==English== {{wp}} ===Etymology=== {{root|en|ine-pro|*dʰeyǵʰ-}} {{dercat|en|itc-pro|ine-pro}} From {{inh|en|enm|feynen}}, {{m|enm|feinen}},{{R:Etymonline}} borrowed from {{der|en|fro|feindre||to pretend}}, from {{der|en|la|fingo|fingere|to [[form]], shape, invent}}. Compare {{cog|fr|feignant|lit=feigning|pos=present participle of {{m|fr|feindre}}}}. Also compare {{m|en|feint}}, {{m|en|figment}} and {{m|en|fiction}}. ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/feɪn/}} * {{audio|en|En-us-fane.ogg|a=US}} * {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vininn126-feign.wav|a=US}} * {{rhymes|en|eɪn|s=1}} * {{homophones|en|fane|foehn|fain}} ===Verb=== {{en-verb}} # To make a [[false]] show or pretence of; to [[counterfeit]] or [[simulate]]. #: {{ux|en|The pupil '''feigned''' sickness on the day of his exam.}} #: {{ux|en|They '''feigned''' her signature on the cheque.}} #: {{co|en|'''feign''' ignorance, '''feign''' illness, '''feign''' indifference, '''feign''' injury, '''feign''' innocence, '''feign''' interest}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1599|author=w:William Shakespeare|title=As You Like It|section=III.iii.18-21 |passage=[T]he truest poetry is the most
feigning, and lovers are given to poetry, and what
they swear in poetry may be said as lovers they do
'''feign'''.}} #* {{RQ:Thackeray Vanity Fair|2|text=She had not been much of a dissembler, until now her loneliness taught her to '''feign'''.}} # To [[imagine]]; to [[invent]]; to [[pretend]] to do something. #: {{ux|en|He '''feigned''' that he had gone home at the appointed time.}} # To make an action as if doing one thing, but actually doing another, for example to trick an opponent; to [[feint]]. #* {{quote-journal|en|year=14 August 2013|author=Daniel Taylor|title=Rickie Lambert's debut goal gives England victory over Scotland|journal=The Guardian|url=http://www.theguardian.com/football/2013/aug/14/england-scotland-international-friendly|text={{w|Gary Cahill|Cahill}} was beaten far too easily for {{w|Kenny Miller|Miller}}'s goal, although the striker deserves the credit for the way he controlled {{w|Alan Hutton}}'s right-wing delivery, with his back to goal, '''feigned''' to his left then went the other way and pinged a splendid left-foot shot into {{w|Joe Hart|Hart}}'s bottom right-hand corner.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20261018032341/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2013/aug/14/england-scotland-international-friendly|archivedate=18 October 2026}} ====Synonyms==== * {{sense|represent by a false appearance}} {{l|en|front}}, {{l|en|put on airs}} * See [[Thesaurus:deceive]] ====Derived terms==== {{col|en|feignable |feigned |feigner |feignful |unfeigned }} ====Translations==== {{trans-top-see|to make a false show|feign|invent}} * Arabic: * Bulgarian: * Catalan: * Chinese: * Czech: * Danish: * Dutch: * Esperanto: * Finnish: * French: * Friulian: * Galician: * German: * Greek: * Hindi: * Hungarian: * Italian: * Japanese: * Lombard: * Lushootseed: * Māori: * Norwegian: * Occitan: * Polish: * Portuguese: * Russian: {{t+|ru|притворя́ться|impf}}, {{t+|ru|прики́дываться|impf}}, {{t+|ru|симули́ровать|impf}}, {{t+|ru|подделывать|impf}} * Scottish Gaelic: * Spanish: * Swedish: * Turkish: * Ukrainian: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top-see|to imagine, to invent, to pretend; to give a mental existence to something|imagine|invent}} * Arabic: * Bulgarian: * Dutch: * Finnish: * Galician: * German: * Hindi: * Hungarian: * Italian: * Māori: * Portuguese: * Russian: {{t+|ru|выду́мывать|impf}} * Scottish Gaelic: * Swedish: * Ukrainian: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|to hide, conceal, or dissemble}} * Arabic: * Bulgarian: * Dutch: * Finnish: * German: * Hungarian: * Italian: * Māori: * Portuguese: * Russian: {{t+|ru|скрыва́ть|impf}}, {{t+|ru|пря́тать|impf}} * Swedish: * Ukrainian: {{trans-bottom}} {{checktrans-top}} * Woiwurrung: {{t-check|wyi|marrnen}} {{trans-bottom}} ===References=== {{reflist}}
